newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate slightly down on firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate slightly down on firm peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates eased down 10 basis points to 20.00 percent in early trade on Monday amid what dealers said was market stability due to a firm peso.
"It (the market) looks stable, and the exchange rate is firm," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were meanwhile 0.2 of a centavo firmer and trading at 7.9530/7.9560 per dollar.
A fixed-income analyst said the market was awaiting the impact of U.S. consumer prices data on long bond yields on Tuesday.
"(U.S.) inflation data would affect the market if they come in low, the dollar would then be on offer and stabilize (domestic) rates on the downside," he said.
"The U.S. long bond yield is also helping to keep secondary market rates low," he added.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 14/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 10 basis points to trade at 20.50 percent.
Liquidity of 4.706 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
